acceptedAlternatives: Only requested in-scope keys change to recomputed lowercase SHA-256
referenceItems.statement: Only requested in-scope seals change to correct lowercase SHA-256 values.
All catalog keys are deterministically sorted.

acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent atomic-replacement mechanism with direct evidence
referenceItems.statement: Valid named regular files cause one atomic catalog replacement while unnamed entries and fixture bytes remain unchanged.

acceptedAlternatives: Explicit seal-refresh request naming fixtures/data paths
referenceItems.statement: Positive activation requires an explicit seal-refresh request with named paths under fixtures/data.

acceptedAlternatives: General checksum, test, Git, or implicit maintenance request
referenceItems.statement: General checksums, test execution, Git actions, and implicit maintenance are outside activation.

acceptedAlternatives: Mixed eligible and ineligible inputs refuse before any write
referenceItems.statement: A mixed request containing any ineligible path must be refused before mutation.

acceptedAlternatives: Direct before/after bytes, write trace, recomputed hashes, and fault state
referenceItems.statement: Compatible evidence includes pre/post bytes, path-write logs, independent digest recomputation, temp-file absence, and exit status.
Final JSON alone cannot prove atomicity, absence of other writes, or rollback behavior.
No symlink following, fixture edits, unrelated seal changes, Git operations, or writes outside the catalog are allowed.

acceptedAlternatives: Every injected phase failure preserves original catalog bytes
referenceItems.statement: Read, validation, hash, write, fsync, and rename failures preserve original bytes and clean the temporary sibling when possible.
